content: Primaquine is a medication used in combination with other drugs to prevent and treat malaria, a disease caused by parasites transmitted through mosquito bites in regions where malaria is prevalent. Malaria parasites can invade the body through mosquito bites and reside in tissues such as red blood cells or the liver. Primaquine is typically administered after other medications, such as chloroquine, have eradicated the parasites within red blood cells. It then targets and eliminates parasites residing in other tissues, thereby preventing the recurrence of the infection. Both primaquine and the initial medication are necessary for a complete cure. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) provides updated guidelines and travel recommendations for malaria prevention and treatment worldwide. To use primaquine, take it orally as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. It should be taken with food to minimize stomach upset. Follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Primaquine is generally taken for two weeks after leaving a malaria-endemic area. It is initiated during the last one to two weeks of other malaria treatment or immediately after completing the other treatment. The dosage depends on the type of infection and your response to treatment. It is crucial to take this medication regularly and exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less than the prescribed amount, and do not stop taking it before completing the treatment, even if you feel better, unless instructed by your doctor. Preventing mosquito bites is essential while taking primaquine. Use insect repellents containing diethyltoluamide (DEET), wear clothing that covers most of your body, stay in air-conditioned or well-screened areas, use mosquito nets, and apply insect-killing sprays. Purchase insect repellents before traveling. No drug treatment is entirely effective in preventing malaria. Seek immediate medical attention if you develop symptoms of malaria, such as fever, chills, headache, or other flu-like symptoms, especially while in a malaria-endemic area or even after completing this prescription. Common side effects of primaquine include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, stomach upset, and abdominal cramps. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar advice. Before taking primaquine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Primaquine may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Primaquine may cause a condition affecting heart rhythm known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs, such as diuretics (water pills), or if you experience severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. Women of childbearing age should undergo a pregnancy test before starting this medication. It is essential to prevent pregnancy during and after treatment with primaquine. Both men and women must use reliable forms of birth control, such as condoms or birth control pills, during treatment. Men should continue using birth control for at least three months after completing treatment, while women should continue for at least one menstrual cycle after treatment ends. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Traveling to malaria-endemic areas during pregnancy significantly increases the risk of death and other complications for both the mother and the infant. The CDC recommends continuing other malaria treatments, such as chloroquine, throughout pregnancy until delivery to prevent harm to the unborn baby, such as hemolytic anemia. After delivery, primaquine treatment may be completed. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Your doctor should test your infant for G6PD deficiency before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and medical tests, such as G6PD blood tests and blood cell counts, should be conducted before starting this medication and during its use. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store primaquine at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
